name: Johnson's Tody-Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Northern peru (cordillera de colán) and adjacent eastern andes
description: Small, colorful flycatcher of Peru’s eastern Andes; found mainly in the northern part of the country, but there is at least one isolated population much farther south. Combination of red head, white chin, gray collar, and yellow belly is distinctive.

name: Banda Sea Pitta
rangeDescription: Seram, watubela, banda, tayandu, kai, and tanimbar islands
description: A typical pitta: plump, short-tailed, long-legged, and primarily terrestrial (sometimes perches up to call). Bright green above with electric blue shoulder patch and rump and black head with conspicuous pale brow.

name: Black-capped Swallow
rangeDescription: Highlands of southern mexico (chiapas) to western honduras
description: Small swallow, rather local in high mountains; found around towns and villages and in pine-oak forests and clearings. Flight fast and “twinkling,” from low over treetops to fairly high overhead; at times perches on wires.

name: Marañon Spinetail
rangeDescription: Southern ecuador (zamora-chinchipe) to northwestern peru (northern cajamarca)
description: Very shy spinetail restricted to the Marañon Valley of northwestern Peru and extreme southern Ecuador; highly threatened due to ongoing habitat loss. Plumage is mostly gray with chestnut back, wings, and tail.

name: Striated Caracara
rangeDescription: Tierra del fuego, staten island, navarino island, and falkland islands
description: Fairly common locally on the Falklands and on remote and largely inaccessible islands south and west of Tierra del Fuego. Habits much like other caracaras; walks with agility to scavenge for food, and sails, soars, and tumbles easily on updrafts.

name: Red-crested Cotinga
rangeDescription: Andes of colombia to western venezuela and western bolivia
description: This plump gray bird is a regular sight atop patches of trees from the temperate forest zone to above treeline in the Andes from Venezuela to Bolivia. The plumage is unremarkable at first glance: both sexes are medium gray with a darker face, blackish wings, and a white band on the tail (visible in flight).

name: Hainan Partridge
rangeDescription: Montane forest of hainan (off southern china)
description: Small game bird restricted to the tropical rainforests of southern Hainan Island, where it is the only forest-dwelling partridge. Body is brown above and gray below; head is black with a bright white ear patch and an orange collar.

name: Sao Tome Paradise-Flycatcher
rangeDescription: São tomé island (gulf of guinea)
description: A distinctive long-tailed paradise-flycatcher with different-looking sexes. Male is glossy blue-black with a pale blue bill and blue eye-rings; female has a dark crown, a gray face, rusty upperparts, and pale underparts.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Ouvea Parakeet
rangeDescription: Loyalty islands (ouvéa)
description: Spectacular, relatively large mostly green parakeet with a black face, slight bit of red on the forehead, and thin but prominent “horns” consisting of a crest made up of a pair of black feathers. Typically found in remnant patches of high-quality forest, but visits more disturbed habitat nearby, especially where fruiting trees are present.

name: Common Sunbird-Asity
rangeDescription: Highland forest of eastern madagascar
description: Tiny, round, short-tailed bird with a long curved bill. Breeding males are blue on the back and yellow below, with bright bare skin around the eye.

name: Rothschild's Swift
rangeDescription: Andes of northwestern argentina; rarely adjacent southern bolivia and peru (cusco)
description: Uncommon swift found along the east slope of the Andes from central Bolivia to northwestern Argentina. Uniform sooty brown, lacking any strong plumage characteristics.

name: Burmese Bushlark
rangeDescription: Central myanmar
description: Speckled brown lark with a thick bill and a short tail. Bright white belly marked with clear dark chest streaking.

name: Amur Falcon
rangeDescription: Steppes of northeastern asia; winters from malawi to south africa
description: The male of this small falcon is sooty gray with rufous-orange thighs and vent. The females are duller gray above, and their white underparts are well marked with dark chevrons.

name: Great Swallow-tailed Swift
rangeDescription: Mountains of southern mexico to southern honduras and (rarely) northern costa rica
description: Large, spectacular swift, seen singly or in small groups (up to 10 birds). Favors drier mountain and foothill areas, often near cliffs, but ranges widely.

name: Chestnut-and-black Weaver
rangeDescription: Varied wooded habitats from guinea to eastern nigeria
description: Males have an unusual and distinctive coloration: mostly black, with a chestnut back and belly. Females are brownish-olive, with paler underparts, and a rufous tinge to the rump.

name: Pearly-bellied Seedeater
rangeDescription: Eastern paraguay to southern brazil (southern mato grosso) and northeastern argentina
description: Very small finchlike bird with a short bill. Inhabits savannas and grasslands, where it often joins flocks of other seedeater species.

name: Plain Leaf Warbler
rangeDescription: Oak-juniper woodland of iran to afghanistan and kashmir
description: A small, unmarked warbler with dark bill and legs. Sandy gray above and pale gray below.

name: Tamarugo Conebill
rangeDescription: Southwestern peru (arequipa and tacna) to northern chile (tarapacá)
description: Very local. Breeds commonly (September to March) in groves of tamarugo trees in the Atacama Desert of northern Chile; most birds then migrate north to foothills of the Andes in northern Chile and southern Peru.

name: Ludwig's Bustard
rangeDescription: Far southwestern angola to namibia, southwestern botswana, and south africa
description: A large-to-medium-sized bustard with a dull orangish nape and hind neck, and dark gray-brown fore neck and face. Female and juvenile are smaller than male and paler on the face and throat.

name: Orange-breasted Sunbird
rangeDescription: Heathlands and protea shrubs of southwestern cape province (south africa)
description: The male is a stunning sunbird with a fiery-orange belly and an iridescent purple breast band and green head. The female and juvenile are dull olive with slightly paler underparts.
